text:
hannah: FYI onboarding run for mistral-lite-26b-quant-v2 started showing intermittent OOMs on multi-turn summarization (mostly long contexts + 2-3 user turns). stack traces show eviction attempts + failed allocs.
hannah: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-22T14:02:11Z] worker-7: alloc slab 4.1GB -> ENOMEM
[2026-03-22T14:02:11Z] runtime: attempted kv_eviction, evicted 0 slots
[2026-03-22T14:02:11Z] runtime: enter slow-path (prefetch miss) stall=95ms
```
sanjay: can you dump the run config and load pattern? curious about batching and max_new_tokens defaults.
hannah: sanitized config below:
```
model: mistral-lite-26b-quant-v2
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  max_clients_in_batch: 6
  microbatch_decouple: false
generation:
  max_new_tokens: 768
  temperature: 0.0
runtime:
  prefetch: true
  kv_reserve_frac: 0.04
  slot_compaction_on_evict: false
```
mike: two immediate smells: max_new_tokens=768 with large max_batch_tokens stretches transient peak allocations, and kv_reserve_frac 0.04 is pretty small for this quantized kernel profile.
elaine: +1. we had a different 26b quant variant where attention intermediate buffers spike during cross-attention in multi-turn flows. microbatch_decouple=true helped with peak concurrency. also enabling slot_compaction_on_evict reduced fragmentation after ~10k requests.
hannah: quick repro matrix: single-client sequential long-prof (3 turns, each ~250 tokens) -> OOM 7/20 runs. set max_new_tokens=512 -> OOM 1/20. set kv_reserve_frac=0.12 (keep others same) -> OOM 0/20. microbatch_decouple=true + max_clients_in_batch=3 -> also eliminated OOMs in our canary.
ryan: good triage. prefer model-level defaults instead of global changes. propose model preset: generation.max_new_tokens=512, runtime.kv_reserve_frac=0.12, batching.microbatch_decouple=true, batching.max_clients_in_batch=3, runtime.slot_compaction_on_evict=true.
sanjay: agree. also add a kernel-level trace for a few failing traces to check which op triggers the blowup (e.g., rotary, flash-attn workspace) before we finalize. may be useful for future quant kernel fixes.
mike: note the tradeoff: lowering max_new_tokens hurts tail of user-required long summaries. if customers need >512 we can allow an explicit per-request override with a rate-limited flag or route to dedicated capacity.
hannah: canary notes (after applying the preset to canary nodes, 1k long-summary requests):
- baseline (pre-preset): p50=44ms p95=1280ms OOMs: 9/1000
- preset (canary): p50=48ms p95=720ms OOMs: 0/1000
- observed slight increase in CPU scheduler work due to microbatch decoupling but overall tokens/sec steady.
elaine: run a quality eval to ensure microbatching doesn't reorder prompts in a way that affects deterministic scoring (we use seed=0, compare rouge). add that to CI for this model.
ryan: CI: added perf+quality gate for mistral-lite-26b-quant-v2: longform-summaries benchmark with 1k samples, compare rouge & latency distributions.
ci-bot: Canary deploy triggered for model-catalog:mistral-lite-26b-quant-v2 -> canary-6 (timeout 1h).
sanjay: also add an alert on oom_counter > 0 for that model in canary so we get immediate paging instead of waiting for daily batch.
hannah: PATCH I pushed to model-catalog (canary-only):
```
PATCH /model-catalog/mistral-lite-26b-quant-v2
{
  "generation.max_new_tokens": "512",
  "runtime.kv_reserve_frac": "0.12",
  "batching.microbatch_decouple": "true",
  "batching.max_clients_in_batch": "3",
  "runtime.slot_compaction_on_evict": "true"
}
```
mike: thumbs_up emoji. after 1h and clean metrics we can promote and document heuristics in onboarding guide: (1) prefer kv_reserve >=0.10 for 26b quant, (2) avoid default >512 new tokens for hosted, (3) use microbatch decoupling for multi-turn summarization workloads, (4) enable slot compaction to reduce slab fragmentation.
elaine: I'll run kernel traces on the failure logs we captured earlier and drop findings in the ticket.
hannah: thanks all 44d I'll keep monitoring, will post final promote decision here.
